items.title: Ethnic unity or mandated monoculture? How a law in China threatens critics in Australia
items.summary: A new law in China requires parents to guide their children to love the Chinese Communist Party, schools to teach a government-approved version of Chinese history, and all citizens to refrain from doing anything the government deems not conducive to promoting a unified Chinese ethnicity. With the laws extending to critics abroad, minority ethnic groups like the Uyghurs and Tibetans say the laws codify and expand longstanding policies of forced assimilation and threaten to silence critics around the world.

items.title: Housing in spotlight as domestic violence crisis continues

It comes as the Second Action Plan to end domestic, family and sexual violence is being developed, in collaboration with a sector under significant strain.

items.title: Ukraine accuses Russia of using North Korean missiles; Zelenskiyy hands new peace proposal to US
items.summary: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskiyy has accused Russia of using North Korean missiles in an attack that killed at least seven people. The President also says he has handed a new proposal to US negotiators for a plan to end the war. It follows the Russian Supreme Court's move to bar the country's only officially-registered anti-war party, and as Ukrainian detainees accuse Russia of systematically torturing prisoners of war.
